title: The Forgotten Spire
premise: Kestrel Halloran guards a sealed gate to the old gods' realm, hiding as a charm-seller in Vharen, a city where magic is punishable by burning. When prayers start being answered again—twisted and hungry—the gate's wards begin failing, and Kestrel learns the country he lives in was erased from the gods' memory long ago; the 'door out' is the only way to restore it. Gathering a found family of outcasts—a disgraced inquisitor, a god-touched child, and a smuggler who once betrayed him—he races across a land that literally forgets itself behind them. At the spire's heart, Kestrel must choose between sealing the gate forever at the cost of his own name, or opening it and trusting the old gods with mercy they've never shown.
about_author: Lior Joubert is a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing banned texts before turning to fiction full-time. They write fantasy about institutions that fail and the people who quietly refuse to let them.

chapters.title: Small Charms
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. In the market city of Vharen, Kestrel sells harmless luck-charms while secretly maintaining the wards on a forgotten gate beneath his shop. A child's prayer is answered by something ancient—and wrong. Emotional beat: quiet dread beneath routine.

chapters.title: The Ash Inquisitor
chapters.summary: Sera Vane's POV. Sera, an inquisitor stripped of rank for heresy, investigates the answered prayer and finds a miracle that killed its recipient. She traces it toward Kestrel's district. Emotional beat: righteous certainty beginning to crack.

chapters.title: What the Wards Remember
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. The gate's wards speak to him for the first time in seven years, showing him a vision of a country that no longer appears on any map—including his own memories of home. Emotional beat: vertigo of lost identity.

chapters.title: A Bargain in Smoke
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. Desperate for answers, Kestrel seeks the smuggler Doss Marrow, who once sold him out to the authorities. Doss agrees to help—for a price: passage through the gate when it opens. Emotional beat: wary, bitter alliance.

chapters.title: The God-Touched Girl
chapters.summary: Sera's POV. Sera arrests a girl named Pell whose prayers are answered instantly and accurately. Instead of burning her, Sera hides her—an act of treason she cannot explain even to herself. Emotional beat: compassion against doctrine.

chapters.title: Doors That Should Stay Shut
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. Sera corners Kestrel; instead of arresting him, she shows him Pell. The three realize the answered prayers are draining the land into the gods' realm. Emotional beat: enemies becoming reluctant allies.

chapters.title: The Country With No Name
chapters.summary: Pell's POV. Traveling east, Pell experiences the forgetting firsthand: villages dissolving, roads unspooling behind them. She alone can still see what was erased. Emotional beat: loneliness of being the only witness.

chapters.title: Salt and Cinders
chapters.summary: Doss's POV. Doss reveals he once worked for the Order that built the spire, and that the gate was never meant to keep gods out—it was meant to keep a promise in. Emotional beat: guilt surfacing after years of deflection.

chapters.title: The Choir of Ash
chapters.summary: Sera's POV. The Order's remnant hunts them, led by Sera's former mentor, Prelate Ossen, who believes feeding the gods will buy salvation. First true battle; Doss is wounded. Emotional beat: Sera choosing her new family over her past.

chapters.title: What Prayers Cost
chapters.summary: Pell's POV. Pell answers a dying farmer's prayer and feels part of herself go with it. Kestrel teaches her to refuse—but refusing means letting people suffer. Emotional beat: the crushing weight of power.

chapters.title: The Hollow City
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. They reach the capital and find it half-forgotten: citizens who cannot remember their own children. Kestrel recognizes his childhood street and cannot remember his mother's face. Emotional beat: grief made literal.

chapters.title: Ossen's Sermon
chapters.summary: Ossen's POV. The prelate offers Kestrel a place at his side, arguing that the old gods are justice itself—law without mercy, order without corruption. Kestrel sees his own fear reflected back. Emotional beat: temptation dressed as principle.

chapters.title: Betrayal at the Ford
chapters.summary: Doss's POV. Cornered by the Order, Doss considers selling them out again—and instead burns his own escape route to save Pell. He takes a blade meant for her. Emotional beat: redemption purchased at real cost.

chapters.title: The Spire Appears
chapters.summary: Pell's POV. The Forgotten Spire rises from the mist, visible only to those the gods have marked. Inside, time pools like water; they walk through moments of their own pasts. Emotional beat: awe laced with terror.

chapters.title: Doors Within Doors
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. Kestrel discovers the gate has many faces—one for every prayer ever answered—and that closing it means erasing every miracle, including the ones that saved lives. Emotional beat: no clean choices left.

chapters.title: The Price of Names
chapters.summary: Sera's POV. To open the true door, someone must give the gods their name as collateral. Sera volunteers, believing her name already belongs to ash. Kestrel refuses to let her. Emotional beat: love stated plainly at last.

chapters.title: Ossen Ascendant
chapters.summary: Ossen's POV. Ossen reaches the summit first and begins feeding the gods an entire congregation of willing faithful, believing sacrifice will remake the world lawful. Emotional beat: conviction curdling into monstrosity.

chapters.title: The Gate Opens
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. Kestrel opens the door and faces the old gods—not monsters, but starving custodians who forgot why they were guarding anything. He gives them not his name but his memory of the gate itself. Emotional beat: surrender as strength.

chapters.title: What the Gods Forgot
chapters.summary: Pell's POV. Pell, the only one who remembers everything, becomes the bridge—teaching the gods the names of the forgotten country one soul at a time. Ossen falls into the closing light, unanswered at last. Emotional beat: small mercies scaling into restoration.

chapters.title: Ashes Settling
chapters.summary: Sera's POV. The land re-members itself; the capital breathes. Sera surrenders to the surviving Order expecting execution, and is instead asked to rebuild it differently. Emotional beat: justice outside the law, finally institutionalized.

chapters.title: A Shop With No Lock
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. Kestrel reopens his shop, now selling honest charms in a country where magic is legal again. Doss, limping, moves in upstairs; Pell calls it home. Emotional beat: found family, settled and warm.

chapters.title: The Keeper's Door
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV, coda. Years later, Kestrel keeps a small unlocked door in his shop floor that leads nowhere—except on nights when someone truly needs it. He leaves a lamp burning. Emotional beat: vigilance transformed into welcome.
